title: Granular run clipboard - micro experiment tracker (Riley)
content:
Purpose:
A compact single-sheet tracker for ad-hoc micro-experiments: quick runs, one-off config tweaks, and shallow comparisons. Meant for fast capture during research sprints and to avoid losing the context of a run.

Table (rows are chronological, newest on top):
| Run ID | Date | Model | Config (short) | Batch | SeqLen | Tokens/run | p50 ms | p95 ms | $/1k tokens | Score/Notes | Next action |
| R-2026-02a | 2026-02-08 | redwood-v2-13B-fp16 | kv-cache:on, q8-compat | 8 | 512 | 7.2k | 120 | 310 | 0.72 | beam outputs slightly repetitive; truncation at prompt boundary | try small prompt rewrite + warmup cache |
| R-2026-01z | 2026-01-29 | open-13B-qlora | kv-cache:off, q4 | 16 | 256 | 3.5k | 95 | 250 | 0.48 | cheaper but p95 spikes on auth-heavy requests | enable aggressive batching for steady streams |
| R-2025-12f | 2025-12-15 | redwood-7B-int8 | kv-cache:on, batch:4 | 4 | 1024 | 10.1k | 85 | 220 | 0.32 | best cost/latency so far for long sequence use | schedule week-long stability run |
| R-2025-11m | 2025-11-05 | gpt-open-6.7B | kv-cache:on, q8 | 8 | 128 | 1.8k | 60 | 140 | 0.90 | high-quality but expensive for short replies | test compact prompt formatting |

Quick notes / heuristic reminders:
- Warmup: 3 warmup requests with typical prefix reduces p95 by ~12% on cached models.
- Batching: for bursty traffic, cap batch size at 8 for <=256 seqlen; larger seqlens benefit from smaller batches to avoid memory thrash.
- Quantization: q4 gives solid cost wins; q8 still useful where slight FP16 ops are faster for medium-seq runs.

Observations from recent runs:
- R-2026-02a: repetition seems tied to prompt tokens near 512 boundary. Suspect attention window and compiled kernel switch.
- R-2026-01z: rare p95 outliers correlate with GC spikes on node - check node-level mem pressure and autoscaler logs.
- R-2025-12f: int8 path very robust but occasionally produces tokenization edge-case errors on emojis/international punctuation.

Short checklist before next run:
- [ ] Add deterministic seed to evaluate exact output differences (where applicable).
- [ ] Attach prompt.txt and gold-response sample to linked artifacts in Confluence.
- [ ] Schedule 24-hour stability run for R-2025-12f config.
- [ ] File bug if p95 outliers reappear with same node id (include node diagnostics).

Scratch ideas / experiment riffs:
- Try tiny-cache-only mode (no KV caching across requests) to see cold-start pattern impact for <128 seq uses.
- Test delta quantization: keep first N layers in fp16 then q4 below for quality-sensitive prompts.
- Probe stop-token handling when combining streaming + function-calls (edge truncation seen in R-2026-02a).

Context links / quick refs:
- Prompt examples saved in Confluence page: /display/ENG/Micro+Run+Logs#Prompts
- Infra investigation PR: GH infra/serving#432 (linked_artifacts)
- Related ticket: JIRA PROBE-789 (p95 memory spikes)

Notes to self (freeform):
- Keep this sheet lean. If an experiment graduates (repeatable, >5 runs, clear signal) move to 'project' folder with full spec.
- When sharing with product/SRE, include cost-per-1k and p95 column only — they care about worst-case and unit economics.

End of sheet.
